newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BA's Ayling backs European airline competitiveness.
newsitem.headline: BA's Ayling backs European airline competitiveness.

text.p: European airlines should not be placed "at a competitive disadvantage vis-a-vis our worldwide rivals, simply by being European-based," British Airways Plc chief executive, Robert Ayling said.
Ayling was quoted in a statement issued by the Association of European Airlines(AEA) following his appointment as AEA's 1997 chairman.
British Airways last held the chair in 1982. Ayling takes over from Herbert Bammer, the president of Austrian Airlines AG.
Ayling's first task is to address the issue of the competitiveness of the European aviation industry in the global marketplace, the AEA statement added.

"The bulk of AEA's members revenue is earned in competition with non-European airlines but subject to the European regulatory framework, they face costs and constraints which are not applicable to their competitors," it said.

It quoted Ayling as saying: "The huge inefficiencies in European air traffic control are already well documented but we have to search out inefficiency and overcharging wherever they exist and demand that out regulators are subject to the same cost discipline as ourselves."

Ayling will head the AEA's presidents' committee whose other members include Jean-Claude Baumgarten of Air France, Pieter Bouw of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Deutsche Lufthansa AG chairman Juergen Weber, Malev chief executive officer Sandor Szathmary, Bammer of AUA, Alitalia chairman Fausto Cereti, and Swissair chief operating officer Philippe Bruggisser.
